title: Locking, Exclusives, and Security Are Different Mechanisms
description: Select each signal to distinguish bus ownership, conditional atomic success, and TrustZone security attribution.

signals.name: HMASTLOCK
signals.description: Requests uninterrupted ownership for a sequence in an arbitrated multi-master context; it does not report exclusive success or security state.
signals.sampled: With address phases belonging to the locked sequence
signals.verificationNote: Check ownership is retained only for the intended sequence and released without starvation.

signals.name: HEXCL
signals.description: Marks an AHB5 exclusive read or write so an exclusive monitor can detect interference without monopolizing the bus.
signals.sampled: With the exclusive transfer address phase
signals.verificationNote: The read and write must target the monitored address and use a consistent transaction identity.

signals.name: HEXOKAY
signals.description: Reports whether an exclusive write actually updated memory. A failed exclusive can still complete with HRESP=OKAY.
signals.sampled: When the exclusive write completes with HREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Never treat HEXOKAY=0 as an HRESP ERROR; it is a conditional atomic failure.

signals.name: HNONSEC
signals.description: Labels the transfer as Secure or Non-secure for TrustZone access control; it does not lock the bus or create atomicity.
signals.verificationNote: Check HNONSEC is routed with the correct transfer and that access denial produces the specified response.
